surface_mechanism_description: The crystal growth mechanism is dominated by the surface nucleated grain density and the Ostwald ripening effect. At lower temperatures (150-250 °C), the grain growth exhibits a negative temperature dependence due to the surface nucleated grain density, allowing sidelong growth without suppression by nearby grain boundaries. At higher temperatures (300-500 °C), the grain growth is dominated by Ostwald ripening, with increased diffusion rates leading to grain coalescence and larger grain sizes.
evidence: According to the results of the foregoing analysis, the crystal growth mechanism of the TiO2 films grown by ALD is dominated by two important factors, the surface nucleated grain density and the Ostwald ripening effect. In the growth temperature range of 150-250 °C, the grain growth exhibits a negative temperature dependence that could be attributed to the surface nucleated grain density. With the lower surface nucleated grain density, there is a sidelong growth process whereby the grain could be enlarged, without being suppressed by the boundaries of nearby grains. In the growth temperature range of 300-500 °C, the grain growth is dominated by Ostwald ripening. In addition, the diffusion rate of the atoms increases along with the increasing temperature, and thus, the grains coalesce more and the grain size is also enlarged.
